panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Front-view 111In-Cl3 SPECT/CT of a human patient with very advanced primary myelofibrosis showing a massively enlarged spleen with very intense radiotracer uptake (splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis), a pattern the authors describe as pathognomonic of PMF. Real patient nuclear-medicine image with clear disease-specific manifestation; yellow arrow annotation present. B: Side-view 111In-Cl3 SPECT/CT of the same human patient with very advanced primary myelofibrosis, confirming the huge spleen with intense radiotracer uptake (splenic EMH) and absent axial skeletal fixation. Real patient nuclear-medicine image directly demonstrating a disease-specific manifestation of PMF; yellow arrow annotation present.

in_text_mentions: In PMF patients, we observed a lower fixation of both tracers 99mTc and 111In‐Cl3 in the axial skeleton and, conversely, a higher fixation in the distal skeleton (Figs. 1 and 2; Table 1). Moreover, using hybrid imaging of 111In‐ Cl3 coupled to SPECT/CT allowed for a more detailed visualization of the extent and intensity of the EMH detected in the spleen of the PMF patients we studied (Fig. 3). In patients with advanced fibrotic process (Fig. 2, patients 1 to 4 and 6), this high splenic uptake was associated to a similar pattern of high 111In‐Cl3 fixation in the distal skeleton.

We consider, the more advanced the process of marrow fibrosis and HSC externalization is, the stronger is the 111In‐Cl3 splenic uptake. In conclusion, when associated with a lower fixation of this same radionuclide in the axial skeleton, the combined pattern of strong 111In‐Cl3 splenic and distal skeletal uptake was highly suggestive and pathognomonic of PMF (Figs. 2 and 3).

Based on our observations, the splenic EMH that was well detected by 111In‐Cl3/SPECT/CT appears to be associated with a high inflammatory process (Fig. 3). We can obtain some evidence of this inflammatory component of PMF from 99mTc nanocolloids/SPECT/CT imaging, which reflects, in part, the activity of several cell types involved in inflammation.
